Do you want to create solutions that ensure the right coordination between sales, production, purchasing and suppliers? Are you passionate about optimizing supply chains and making logistics run smoothly? Are you looking for an internship at an international green tech company, with the opportunity to start earlier as a student worker?

Here is what your role entails

As our intern in Planning & Logistics you will be supporting our three core functions: Production Planning, Operational Purchasing, and Shipping, that ensures timely flow of materials and products from suppliers to our own production facilities. You will be contributing to efficient planning and continuous improvement across our supply chain.

More specifically, you will be:

• Participating in meetings with production teams and contributing to short- and midterm production planning

• Assisting our purchasers with various procurement processes and helping the Shipping team in planning and executing shipments

• Engaging in improvement projects across our internal workflows together with the logistics and planning specialists

• Conducting data analyses and tracking progress on project-related activities

As our Intern, you will gain hands-on experience across key supply chain disciplines, building a solid understanding of how planning, purchasing, and logistics work together to support business operations. From day one, you will be entrusted with meaningful responsibilities, while working on tasks that support your professional development. Moreover, you will do so while receiving guidance and support from experienced colleagues.

Meet your future team

During your internship you will become part of our Planning & Logistics Department joining a team consisting of 7 dedicated colleagues with expertise in various logistics tasks across shipping, purchasing and production planning. Collaboration is a core element in our team where we value knowledge-sharing and strive to always be one step ahead. The close collaboration with your experienced colleagues gives you a unique opportunity for sparring and professional growth.

Less about us, more about you

We are looking for a curious student who is ready to learn and eager to apply their knowledge about planning and logistics. Through your studies, you have developed a strong analytical mindset, enabling you to coordinate with suppliers and production planners. As a person you feel comfortable in a collaborative environment and excited about building internal and external relationships at all organizational levels.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Are currently studying Supply Chain, Logistics, or another relevant field

• Have a structured approach to your work that helps you maintain an overview in a dynamic environment with many ongoing tasks

• Possess an analytical mindset and enjoy working with data to support decisions and improvements

• See opportunities rather than limitations making you motivated to challenge existing processes with fresh perspective

As we are an international organization it is important that you are fluent in English and Danish.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, this is an internship position, and we value curiosity and a willingness to learn just as much as experience. If the role interests you and you are motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply.

We offer more than just an internship

At Kamstrup, your contribution as an intern is highly valued, and we cherish the good colleagueship. Therefore, you will experience an internship with a strong focus on your individual development through challenging tasks, career sparring, voluntary courses, as well as social events and a large network. We are proud, that our internship program has resulted in Studenterhus Aarhus granting us with the Mentor Award, the Internationalization Award, the Jury’s Special Award and the award for East Jutland’s Best Internship.

Besides the best program, we also offer:

• A gratuity which may be provided in recognition of your efforts if your place of study allows it as well as paid public transportation to and from work

• Multiple internship events and weekly internship lunches

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association, that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

The applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, but you can expect a response within six weeks. Any details about the internship will be individually agreed upon. However, the internship is expected to run from the beginning of February 2027 until the end of June 2027. You will also have the opportunity to join the department as a student worker prior to your internship, ensuring a smooth transition into the role.

Kamstrup is located in Stilling south of Aarhus, and bus number 200 takes you right to the door.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Senior Manager, Planning & Logistics, H/C SC, Christian Brogaard Nielsen, on phone: +45 89 93 10 00.

jobs.occupation: Experienced Hardware Engineer: Lead the integration of the hardware that powers ambitious satellite missions
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Hardware Engineer to drive the integration, technical ownership, and continuous improvement of the hardware platforms that enable GomSpace's satellite missions.

You will join our Satellite Systems Business Unit in Aalborg and play a central role in supporting satellite missions from proposal and electrical design through assembly, integration, testing, and delivery to customers worldwide. You will work closely with hardware designers, systems engineers, AIV engineers, manufacturing teams, and project managers while helping shape the future development of our hardware engineering capabilities.

Your Role

As experienced Hardware Engineer, you will act as the technical lead for the integration of electrical hardware and GomSpace products into satellite platforms.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Own the technical integration of GomSpace products into nanosatellite and microsatellite missions.

• Serve as a product expert for GomSpace hardware platforms, interfaces, functionality, configuration, and performance.

• Drive technical troubleshooting and root-cause analysis during development, integration, testing, and customer projects.

• Lead the integration and verification of new GomSpace products and third-party hardware within satellite platforms.

• Define electrical interface solutions, schematic-level designs, harness concepts, and supporting hardware required for mission integration.

• Coordinate prototyping, validation, documentation, and manufacturing introduction activities for new hardware solutions.

• Provide technical leadership and mentorship to junior and mid-level engineers.

• Support technical decision-making and trade-off analyses across customer programmes and internal developments.

• Contribute to process improvements, engineering standards, and product maturity initiatives across the organisation.

• Support proposal activities and customer discussions by providing credible technical solutions, effort estimates, and engineering input.

• Prepare technical documentation and communicate effectively in English, including technical reports, specifications, procedures, and interactions with international stakeholders.

What Success Looks Like

In the initial phase, success means:

• Becoming a recognised technical expert on GomSpace's hardware portfolio.

• Successfully leading hardware integration activities on active customer missions.

• Resolving complex technical issues through systematic troubleshooting and engineering analysis.

• Building strong working relationships with Satellite Systems HW Team, Products HW Team, AIV, Manufacturing, and Systems Engineering.

• Supporting the growth and development of less experienced engineers.

Over time, you will be recognised as a trusted technical authority for hardware integration and product implementation, driving engineering excellence and helping scale GomSpace's hardware capabilities as our missions and teams continue to grow.

What You Bring

You are an experienced hardware engineer who enjoys solving technically demanding challenges and transforming complex products into reliable space systems.

You likely bring:

• An MSc or BSc in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Mechatronics, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline.

• 10+ years of experience in hardware design, hardware integration, electronics development, verification, or systems integration.

• Strong knowledge of digital electronics, embedded hardware, and microcontroller-based systems.

• Experience with hardware communication interfaces and buses, including RS485/-422, CAN, SPI, I²C, USB, Ethernet, Spacewire, or similar.

• Experience in schematic capture and hardware development using tools such as Altium Designer or equivalent.

• Understanding of PCB design principles, EMC-, grounding- and shielding considerations, manufacturing processes, and product industrialisation.

• Experience with electrical integration, harness design, laboratory testing, and troubleshooting.

• Practical understanding of power systems, communication systems, and embedded electronics.

• Experience working with multidisciplinary engineering teams and complex technical projects.

• Knowledge of space systems and ECSS standards would be a strong advantage.

• Experience leading technical activities, mentoring engineers, or coordinating engineering teams would be considered a significant benefit.

Who You Are

You are pragmatic, technically curious, and motivated by solving challenging engineering problems.

You are known for:

• Technical leadership – providing direction and guidance without necessarily having formal authority.

• Systems thinking – understanding how individual hardware components contribute to mission success.

• Problem solving – methodically analysing issues and driving them to resolution.

• Collaboration – building strong relationships across engineering disciplines.

• Ownership – taking responsibility for delivering results.

• Mentorship – helping colleagues develop and grow.

• Customer focus – understanding that engineering excellence is measured by mission success.

• True leadership – setting standards, building trust, and enabling others to perform at their best.

Why Join Us

You will play a key role in delivering some of Europe's most ambitious nanosatellite and microsatellite missions, working at the intersection of product development, systems engineering, and customer delivery.

This position offers the opportunity to influence technical decisions across multiple programmes, shape future hardware capabilities, and grow into broader technical or people leadership responsibilities as both the team and business continue to expand.

jobs.occupation: Experienced Systems Engineer – Architecting Nanosatellite & Microsatellite Systems (DK/LU)
jobs.description:
Do you want to own the technical integrity of a mission from "blank sheet" to flight-ready hardware?

GomSpace is seeking a Lead Systems Engineer to drive our next generation of Nanosatellite and Microsatellite missions. We are looking for a technical visionary who thrives on solving complex system trade-offs for both bespoke single-satellite missions and scaling constellation architectures. In this role, you will navigate the newest market developments, helping our customers transition from initial technology demonstrators to operational fleets.

Since 2007, GomSpace has developed and delivered satellites to customers across more than 60 countries worldwide through technological innovation and the efforts of our highly skilled team.

You will have the chance to be part of an international and dedicated team committed to providing exceptional and innovative small-satellite solutions to customers in the global market. Your objectives will be aligned with your personal development goals, and you will be given the autonomy to lead others towards the same direction.

About the Job

As a Lead Systems Engineer in the Satellite Systems Business Unit, you are the technical heart of the mission. You aren’t just managing requirements; you are architecting the system and ensuring its physical realization. You will bridge the gap between customer vision and engineering execution, guiding teams through the full development lifecycle. You will have the autonomy to make high-impact technical decisions across a diverse portfolio, ensuring exceptional performance for single spacecraft and emerging constellation projects.

Responsibilities include:

• Defining and Architecting end-to-end missions, scaling designs from high-performance single satellites to repeatable constellation architectures.

• Driving the full development lifecycle, from proposal response and mission analysis to design, assembly, integration, and testing (AIT).

• Serving as the Technical Authority in front of the customer, translating complex needs into robust system specifications and verifiable requirements.

• Process Excellence: Designing and implementing value-added engineering processes that maintain high quality without sacrificing the speed required in an agile "New Space" environment.

• Leading and Mentoring project systems teams to solve the industry’s toughest challenges in power, thermal, and high-precision pointing.

• Managing complex interfaces and risk profiles, ensuring seamless integration between payload, bus, and launch providers.

Your profile

You are a driven and dedicated professional with a strong focus on delivering high-quality, advanced solutions. You thrive in collaborative and agile environments.

• Proven Experience: Significant years in a Lead or Senior Systems role within the space industry. Experience taking a satellite through the full "design-to-test" lifecycle is essential.

• Process Champion: You have a deep understanding of where to focus effort in the engineering process. You are skilled at implementing streamlined workflows that add genuine value and encourage team adoption in fast-paced environments.

• The "System" Thinker: You understand how a single component change can affect mission-level link budgets, thermal margins, or mass properties.

• Cross-Disciplinary Communicator: Comfortable discussing software configurations with developers, high-speed data links with RF engineers, structural margins with mechanical leads, etc.—everything that goes into a satellite solution.

• Leadership through Action: You foster a culture of helpfulness and open communication, leading by example in both technical depth and professional integrity.

This position is based in Denmark (Aalborg) or Luxembourg (Esch-sur-Alzette). The expected travel activity is 15 -40 days per year, and we are highly receptive to international applicants.

Qualifications:

• MSc-level (or higher) engineering education in aerospace, systems, software, electrical engineering, or related fields.

• Mastery of ECSS/NASA standards, with the ability to tailor these processes to be effective and agile.

• Expertise in systems engineering principles, including requirements management, architecture, and system-level verification and testing.

• Proficiency in mission analysis tools (e.g., STK, GMAT) for coverage, revisit, and orbital analysis.

• Demonstrated ability to design and drive engineering processes that improve team efficiency and product reliability.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify, assess, and mitigate technical risks in space missions or projects.

• Excellent English communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to explain complex concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.

Why choose GomSpace?

• Growth: Providing leadership within a leading space-industry company where innovation and advanced technologies are used to make a positive societal impact.

• Impact: Working alongside passionate, skilled, and international colleagues, driven by curiosity about “New Space” opportunities.

• Culture: Operating in a dynamic and cooperative culture with transparent communication and multidisciplinary teams.

• Network: Learning and growing through the company’s global network of locations and partnerships.

• International: Being part of project work based on international standards and team-oriented approaches.

We are looking for a Domain Architect to join our Business Engagement and Platform Solutions team, where you will take domain ownership of the application and platform architecture and drive alignment across our architecture practices.

About the job

The role combines architectural ownership with close business engagement. You will define and maintain the target architecture for applications and platforms, contribute to solution design together with our solution architects and delivery teams, and act as a trusted architectural advisor to the business areas you support.

Your key responsibilities

• Take domain ownership of Orifarm's application and platform architecture, including current state, target state and the roadmap between them

• Engage closely with business stakeholders to understand their processes, priorities and ambitions, and translate these into application and platform solutions

• Drive the architecture forum by setting the agenda, preparing decisions and ensuring alignment across the solution, data, integration and infrastructure architecture practices

• Support solution architects and delivery teams through design reviews, architectural guidance and joint solution design

• Develop and maintain reference architectures, design patterns and architectural standards for the application and platform domain

• Drive simplification of the application portfolio through consolidation, lifecycle management and modernization of key applications

• Support the evaluation, selection and integration of new applications and platforms, ensuring that they can be operated and maintained sustainably

Who are you?

We are looking for a pragmatic and business-oriented architect who is comfortable moving between technical design and stakeholder dialogue. You communicate clearly, and you create alignment through collaboration and professional credibility.

We imagine your profile includes:

• +5 years of experience within solution, application or platform architecture, or a background as a senior developer, lead engineer with relevant architectural experience

• Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into concrete application and platform solutions

• Good understanding of cloud platforms, preferably Microsoft Azure, as well as ERP ecosystems and modern integration patterns

• Experience facilitating architectural decisions across teams and disciplines, for example through design reviews or architecture forums

• Experience from a regulated industry such as pharmaceuticals, life science or medical devices is an advantage

• Knowledge of architecture frameworks is an advantage, with emphasis on practical application rather than formal certification

• Professional proficiency in English. Danish or German is an advantage

Who are we?

You will be part of Business Engagement & Platform Solutions, a function of approximately 40 colleagues across three business-aligned solution teams as well as architecture and integration practices with direct reference to the VP of Corporate IT. We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. Across teams, functions, and markets, you will find a collaborative and supportive culture built on trust, respect, and a flat hierarchy where everyone has a voice and direct access to decision-makers.

We encourage everyone to apply

Our commitment is to create an environment where different perspectives and skills drive innovation and contribute to a sustainable future. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

The job

Group IT (GRIT) supports Systematic’s business units with infrastructure, systems, integrations, applications and governance. Our Plan-Build-Run model combines sprint-based development, stage-gate projects and Kanban operations to manage and improve services. As IT Portfolio & Capacity Manager, you will connect these delivery models into a trusted view of delivery, commitments and available capacity.

This is a hands-on role, reporting is a part of it, but not all of it. You will work with project managers, delivery teams, architects and leadership, and turn portfolio realities into clear priorities, capacity views, dependencies, risks and delivery expectations. You will move between portfolio decisions with the CIO and GRIT leadership and detailed reviews of project plans or Jira data with delivery teams, challenging commitments, dependencies and capacity assumptions. Your insight will help leadership decide what to prioritise, take on next or defer.

In addition to that, some of your key tasks will be to:

• Create a decision-ready portfolio view across stage-gate projects, sprints and Kanban, keeping commitments, dependencies and decisions visible across Plan-Build-Run.

• Connect demand, commitments and capacity to test delivery feasibility, assessing new demands with the Enterprise Architect and Director of Group IT Strategy.

• Investigate Jira and other delivery data, resolving gaps and inconsistencies with colleagues to establish a trusted portfolio picture.

• Validate progress, plans, dependencies and capacity assumptions directly with project managers and delivery teams, challenging commitments beyond status reports.

• Prepare and facilitate leadership discussions on portfolio priorities, making the impact on existing work, dependencies and capacity clear and following through on decisions and actions.

• Improve portfolio processes and tooling, using automation and AI to reduce manual administration and strengthen transparency and decision support.

Joining the team

The portfolio and capacity management model you will work with is still evolving, and you will play an important role in shaping it. Our ambition is not to build a large administrative PMO. We want a lightweight and trusted portfolio capability that gives us transparency across demand and delivery, helps us make realistic commitments, and enables us to adjust priorities as our capacity and business needs change.

You will become part of the GRIT Strategy team, a small team working across strategy, Enterprise Architecture, portfolio and project management to keep Group IT focused on the right priorities and strengthen the connection between planning and execution. Reporting to the Director of Group IT Strategy, you will take over a running portfolio process from an interim consultant and work closely with project managers, Enterprise Architecture and GRIT leadership.

The team is based in Aarhus. If you are located in Copenhagen, we are open to discussing a hybrid arrangement, but you should expect regular presence in Aarhus, approximately 6–8 days per month.

Your qualifications - most importantly, you understand how work actually gets delivered in an IT organisation.

You have worked close enough to technology delivery to understand the interaction between demand, projects, agile teams, dependencies, capacity and operational commitments. You understand that different teams may plan and deliver work differently, and you are able to create transparency across that complexity without trying to force everything into one delivery model. Your background could be in IT portfolio management, technology delivery, programme management, IT transformation or a PMO role closely integrated with IT delivery. The exact title matters less than your ability to understand delivery and turn fragmented information into a portfolio that can be actively managed. We expect you to have experience with several of the following:

• Experience from portfolio management, IT delivery, programme management, technology transformation or a similar role within an IT organisation.

• A practical understanding of project-based delivery, Scrum/sprint-based delivery and Kanban, and the ability to navigate between these ways of working.

• Experience creating portfolio or capacity views across multiple teams, projects or delivery models.

• The analytical ability to connect demand, capacity, dependencies, commitments and delivery.

• The willingness and ability to work hands-on with the underlying data rather than relying on a separate PMO or reporting organisation to produce it for you.

• Practical experience with Jira or similar delivery management tools.

• Strong analytical capabilities using Excel, Power BI or comparable tools to investigate data and create useful management views.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to turn complex delivery information into clear choices and trade-offs for senior stakeholders.

• Curiosity about how AI and automation can reduce manual portfolio administration and improve decision support.

• Fluent English. Danish is an advantage.

You are structured, curious and persistent

When the portfolio picture is unclear, you do not simply wait for someone to produce another status report. You look into the underlying information, talk to the people involved, challenge assumptions and work out what is actually happening. You enjoy creating order from complexity and are comfortable moving between strategic discussions and delivery detail. You also have the confidence to challenge when things do not add up. If commitments exceed available capacity, dependencies have been overlooked or different sources tell different stories, you make that visible and help the organisation resolve it.

At the same time, you are pragmatic. You understand that perfect data rarely exists in a fast-moving IT organisation and know how to create sufficient transparency to enable decisions without turning portfolio management into bureaucracy. You thrive as a senior specialist who takes ownership of your domain and leads through sound judgement, structure, collaboration and follow-through.

Senior Process Automation Engineer in DCS, Novo Nordisk Engineering

Do you want to be a part of NNE’s all-time largest Process Automation team? We are looking for colleagues to join our fantastic company, where we have the aspiration of becoming best in class within Automation Solutions for Pharmaceutical Engineering.

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

We are skilled in a broad range of process areas within API production e.g. fermentation, recovery and purification, utility, and cleaning systems. • Advising customers on their application process solutions

• Design developing, programming, commissioning, qualifying, FAT, SAT, UAT and Handover of applications for Distributed Control Systems (DCS)

• Interacting with process experts and colleagues with expertise in surrounding systems and equipment like MES, Historian systems, instruments, production equipment etc.

• Developing and optimizing automation methods and strategies to meet our customers’ needs and sharing working knowledge with colleagues and partners

Who you are

• Understand your colleagues’ individual and cultural difference

• Are agile and able to prioritize urgent tasks

• Are team-oriented and able to collaborate on team projects

• Are reliable, curious and eager to learn

The preferred candidate has the following profile:

• Experience from oilfield, energy sector, hydraulics, precision mechanics, electro mechanical systems, mechatronics or similar is a plus

• Agile Project Management skills

• Is experienced in the use of FEA simulations in ANSYS or similar system

• Monitor positions, manage risk, and respond to changing market conditions.

• Strong analytical skills and a solid understanding of trading strategies and risk management.

• The ability to make well-founded decisions under pressure.

• Good communication skills and an interest in sharing knowledge with colleagues.

• A relevant degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering or a related field.

You should be comfortable working in a 24/7 shift rotation and ready to apply your trading experience from an early stage.

You will become part of a specialist trading environment where colleagues share market knowledge, discuss trading ideas, and learn from each other's experience. Beyond the trading desk, you will be part of Norlys Energy Trading's wider professional and social community, including an active staff association that brings colleagues together across teams.

The position is permanent, full-time and based at our office in Aalborg, with an expected start date of 1 February 2027.

jobs.description:
The Position:

The UNFPA Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU) is seeking candidates for its newly established Supply Chain Internship Roster 2026. These internship opportunities are on-site at SCMU’s office in the UN City headquarters in Copenhagen, Denmark.

SCMU offers specialized functional streams aligned with its operational needs, including:

• Data & Analytics

• Logistics & Supply Chain

• Procurement & Business

• Humanitarian Supplies

• Supply Chain & Customer Service

• Governance, Risk & Compliance

• Communications

• Human Resources

• Information and Communications Technology (ICT)

• Administration & Business

To ensure effective team integration and maximize the value of the internship, candidates must be logistically and financially prepared to undertake full-time, on-site work in Copenhagen for the duration of the internship.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead UN agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is wanted, every childbirth is safe and every young person's potential is fulfilled.  UNFPA’s strategic plan (2026-2029), reaffirms the relevance of the current strategic direction of UNFPA and focuses on three transformative results: to end preventable maternal deaths; end unmet need for family planning; and end gender-based violence and harmful practices. These results capture our strategic commitments on accelerating progress towards realizing the ICPD and SDGs in the Decade of Action leading up to 2030. Our strategic plan calls upon UN Member States, organizations and individuals to “build forward better”, while addressing the negative impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic on women’s and girls’ access to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights, recover lost gains and realize our goals.

The UNFPA Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU) is self-funded and was made operational in January 2022. It is tasked with ensuring that UNFPA is able to effectively and efficiently support the delivery of life-saving reproductive health products and other programme supplies to the end user when and where they are needed. To achieve this, it is important to strengthen the capacity of governments and implementing partners to ensure coordination, end-to-end visibility and accountability on all supply chain and logistics management related activities, in particular for programme supplies, across all UNFPA programmes.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff, who embody these international norms and standards, and who will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates that transform, inspire and deliver high impact and sustained results; we need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them and who commit to deliver excellence in programme results.

Eligibility:

Educational requirements

a. Be enrolled in a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent) and have completed one full academic year;

b. Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as master’s programme or higher);

c. Have recently graduated with a university degree as defined above and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation; or

d. Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional trainee programme and undertake the internship as part of this programme.

Other eligibility requirements

e. Demonstrate interest in the field of development;

f.  Demonstrate written and spoken proficiency in at least one of the working languages of the United Nations (English or French) and fluency in the official language (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian or Spanish) of the UNFPA office; and

g. Demonstrate ability to adapt to new environments and to establish and maintain good working relations with individuals of different cultural backgrounds.

An individual whose father, mother, son, daughter, brother or sister is a UNFPA staff member is not eligible for an internship with UNFPA.

Required Competencies:

Values:

• Exemplifying integrity,

• Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,

• Embracing cultural diversity,

• Embracing change

Core Competencies:

• Achieving results,

• Being accountable,

• Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen,

• Thinking analytically and strategically,

• Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships,

Financial Support:

Interns who do not receive financial support from an outside party (such as an academic institution, university, government) are eligible to receive a stipend as a contribution towards living expenses. The stipend is based on the intern’s agreed place of work, which may be different from the duty station of the hiring office in cases of remote arrangements. The stipend is normally paid in local currency at the end of each month.

UNFPA Work Environment:

UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance. We are committed to ensuring gender parity in the organization and therefore encourage women to apply. Individuals from the LGBTQIA+ community, minority ethnic groups, indigenous populations, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. UNFPA promotes equal opportunities in terms of appointment, training, compensation and selection for all regardless of personal characteristics and dimensions of diversity. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of UNFPA's workforce - click here to learn more.

Disclaimer:

UNFPA does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process and does not concern itself with information on applicants' bank accounts.

jobs.occupation: Director Specialist – Key Account Management (Power & Controls)
jobs.description:
Director Specialist – Key Account Management (Power & Controls)

Build strategic partnerships that power the future of renewable energy

At KK Group, we are on an ambitious journey to enable a future powered by renewable energy. We are looking for a commercially driven and relationship-oriented leader to take ownership of a key strategic account and help unlock its full potential.

In this role, you will work at the heart of our business—connecting customers, technology, and operations—to drive sustainable growth, strengthen long-term partnerships, and deliver real impact.

Highlights of the offer

• Job offer expiration: 30/11/2026

• Type of work: Hybrid

• Role: Individual Contributor / Specialist

• Location: Europe, Denmark, Ikast

Responsibilities

Key Account Management:

• Obtain detailed knowledge of the account’s organization, their product portfolio, their on-going projects, and secure this is shared across commodities.

• Identify cooperation and sales opportunities

• Process customer RFQ’s and work cross-functionally with colleagues to generate the best technical and commercial offering

• Process ideas targeting increased business right from idea to implementation. Painstakingly drive the idea internally, build the business case and sell the new product or service

• Keep a strong and tight relationship with the Accounts’ technical and commercial organization and their internal stakeholders

• Contribute in development and adjustment of account strategy in order to support the overall business plan and targets for the account

• Support the customer on a day-to-day business

• Secure correct reporting, data and pipeline management in e.g. CRM

• Support all operational activities where sales need to be involved towards the customers to ensure highest level of performance.

• Drive customer negotiations to land new business and/or supporting the Key Account commodities across.

• Secure timely preparation, process and level of RFQ and negotiations across Key Account commodities and divisions.

Our requirements

We are looking for a commercially strong and collaborative professional who thrives in a global, customer-focused environment.

• 6-10 years of proven experience in Key Account Management within large OEM environments, with a proven ability to drive growth and create value for both the customer and the business

• A basic understanding of electromechanical components and industrial environments

• Strong commercial and financial acumen, with experience in budgeting, performance management, and delivering on business targets

• Excellent stakeholder management and negotiation skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships and align expectations across internal and external partners

• Proven experience in leading cross-functional teams and managing complex projects in an industrial or technical environment

• A structured, analytical, and data-driven mindset, enabling you to translate insights into impactful decisions

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to influence and engage stakeholders at all levels in a global setting

• A collaborative and inclusive leadership style, with a commitment to safety, quality, and company values

• Cross-cultural awareness and the ability to operate effectively in an international matrix organisation

• Fluency in Danish and English (written and spoken); additional languages are considered a plus

Location

This role can be based in our offices in Ikast or Hammel, with flexibility for hybrid work.

Ready to make an impact?

If you are excited about shaping strategic partnerships and contributing to the renewable energy transition, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now & send us your resume in English.

Due to the summer vacation period in Denmark, all applications will be processed only in the beginning of August.

We offer

By joining KK Group, you will be part of a culture where diversity is embraced, every nationality is respected, and trust and collaboration across perspectives drives our success. Across our global organisation, we offer a wide range of job opportunities spanning office-based roles, production facilities, and onsite positions worldwide. Our roles cover multiple functions, locations, and disciplines, providing diverse career paths across the business. Whether you’re interested in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or support functions, you’ll find opportunities at KK Group to grow your skills, contribute to meaningful work, and make an impact.

Potential Benefits (Depending on Role)

Further information

If the above matches your field of interest and your qualifications, please send your application and resume as soon as possible. Interviews are held on an ongoing basis.

For further information, please contact:

Karen Lim  +45 4194 6883

About KK Group

KK Group is a global technology partner delivering power, controls, cooling, monitoring and service solutions for renewable energy and energy-intensive industries.

With more than 45 years of experience in the wind industry and technologies installed in over 120,000 turbines worldwide, KK Group provides critical electro-mechanical systems that enable electrification, improve energy efficiency, and optimise the lifetime performance of industrial assets.

The company’s capabilities span the full value chain - from development and manufacturing to service and digital solutions - supporting customers across the entire lifecycle of their platforms. Backed by its long-term owner, A.P. Moller Holding, KK Group is expanding beyond wind into selected energy-intensive industries including hydrogen, mining, rail and defence.

Today, KK Group employs more than 3,700 people across 10+ countries and is building a more diversified, resilient and global business - Powering Change towards a more sustainable tomorrow.

Visit www.kkgroup.com to learn more about our company and career opportunities.
